newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50-private.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50-private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher amid outlooks for sharply higher CME pork complex futures following Friday's bullishly construed USDA quarterly hogs and pigs report, livestock dealers said.
The report showed U.S. farmers as of June 1 had held back fewer hogs for breeding purposes than expected .
Hogs kept for breeding were pegged at 101 percent of a year ago, below analysts' average pre-report estimate of 104.3 percent and well below the range of estimates of 103-106 percent, USDA said.
All hogs as of June 1 was 102 percent, nearly matching the pre-report estimate of 102.9 percent, and hogs kept for marketing was 102 percent versus an average estimate of 102.6.
Support was seen muffled by light demand from packers going into next Friday's Independence Day holiday, said Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa.
"It's going to be a short week, and I don't think anyone's in a hurry to buy anything," Maher said.
Interior Iowa top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen at $60.00 and Illinois top prices at the plant were seen $59.00 to $59.50. Indiana/Ohio tops could reach $60.50.
